text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Armed Islamic Group (GIA) chief Antar Zouabri trapped or may even have been killed by Algerian troops. Some sources say mass grave with about 100 bodies has been found by advancing troops but it still not known if these are the bodies of civilians or "terrorists" killed in the first days of the operation.

- GIA chief Zouabri, aged 27 and with price of 450,000 dinars ($8,035) on his head, trapped by troops. He has threatened fellow rebels who might think of giving themselves up. "Moreover, the bloody terrorist chief had not hesitated to kill 12 of his close aides who were preparing to surrender." Total of 64 "terrorists" have been killed and 32 surrendered with their weapons in less than a week.
- Antar Zouabri, head of the GIA, is living his last hours.
- Total of 54 people have been assassinated in the Mitidja area in the last three nights, including 35 who had their throats cut in one village.

- President Liamine Zeroual sets October 23 as date for local elections, completing the process of national rebuilding which started in November 1995 with the presidential elections and was followed by the parliamentary election last month.
